_meta.title: Canada: police-reported hate crime by census metropolitan area
_meta.what: Number of hate crime incidents reported by police and the rate per 100,000 people, for each census metropolitan area (CMA), 2014-2025. Each point sits on the core city of the CMA (Wikidata coordinates); the figure is for the whole CMA as policed.
_meta.source: Statistics Canada, Table 35-10-0191-01 Police-reported hate crime, number of incidents and rate per 100,000 population, Census Metropolitan Areas
_meta.citation: Statistics Canada. Table 35-10-0191-01 Police-reported hate crime, number of incidents and rate per 100,000 population, Census Metropolitan Areas. DOI: https://doi.org/10.25318/3510019101-eng

not available for a specific reference period
status_legend.x: suppressed to meet the confidentiality requirements of the Statistics Act

notes.1: Hate crimes refer to criminal offences committed against a person or property that is motivated in whole or in part by bias, prejudice or hate based on race, national or ethnic origin, language, colour, religion, sex, age, mental or physical disability, sexual orientation or gender identity or expression, or on any other similar factor. For more information on the concepts, methods and quality of the data contained in this table, consult the statistical data documentation: Uniform Crime Reporting Survey - 3302.
notes.2: Data for previous years are available upon request. For further details, contact the Canadian Centre for Justice and Community Safety Statistics at statcan.ccjcss-ccsjsc.statcan@statcan.gc.ca.
notes.3: Over the past two decades, police services across Canada have continued to advance their identification and reporting of hate crime incidents. Changes in reporting practices can have an effect on hate crime statistics. For example, an increase in the number of hate crime incidents reported can be influenced by the introduction of a hate crime awareness campaign.
notes.4: This data table replaces CANSIM table 252-0091 which is now archived.
notes.5: Data coverage for police-reported data varies slightly each year. Hate crime data for 2025 covers 99.6% of the Canadian population. Coverage for each province/territory is virtually 100% with the exception of New Brunswick (90.9%) due to the exclusion of Saint John Police Force. These percentages are based on police-reported data and populations for the 2025 data cycle.
notes.6: A census metropolitan area (CMA) consists of one or more neighbouring municipalities situated around a major urban core. A CMA must have a total population of at least 100,000, of which 50,000 or more live in the urban core. To be included in the CMA, other adjacent municipalities must have a high degree of integration with the central urban core, as measured by commuting flows derived from census data. A CMA typically comprises more than one police service. CMA populations have been adjusted to follow policing boundaries. The Oshawa CMA is excluded from this analysis owing to the incongruity between the police service jurisdictional boundaries and the CMA boundaries.  Lethbridge, Alberta and Belleville, Ontario became new CMAs as of the 2016 Census. Fredericton, New Brunswick; Drummondville, Quebec; Red Deer, Alberta; Kamloops, British Columbia; Chilliwack, British Columbia and Nanaimo, British Columbia became new CMAs as of the 2021 Census. Coverage for each CMA is virtually 100%, except in Toronto (approx. 90%), and Hamilton (approx. 76%).
notes.7: Includes Halton Regional Police Service and Durham Regional Police Service. May include a small number of offences that occurred outside of a Census metropolitan area (CMA) as 3% of the population policed by Durham Regional Police Service falls outside the boundaries of a CMA.
notes.9: Excludes the portion of Halton Regional Police Service that polices the Hamilton census metropolitan area (CMA).
notes.10: Part way through 2013, the Royal Canadian Mounted Police revised policing boundaries for rural detachments in New Brunswick. This resulted in a change in the census metropolitan area (CMA) boundaries that are determined for the purpose of reporting crime statistics. As such, 2013 data for the New Brunswick CMAs of Saint John and Moncton are not comparable to previous or future years. Further, data from 2014 onward are not comparable to years prior to 2014.
notes.12: Excludes the portions of Halton Regional Police Service and Durham Regional Police Service that police the Toronto census metropolitan area (CMA).
notes.13: Excluded from this table are the small number of police services that do not report to the Uniform Crime Reporting Survey (UCR) 2. With the exception of Lasalle Police Service  (included in Windsor CMA), Kahnawake Mohawk Peacekeepers ( Montreal CMA), Six Nations Police Service (Brantford CMA) and Dalmeny Police Service (Saskatoon CMA)  in 2017, who provided data through special submission.
notes.14: Police data on hate crimes reflect only the incidents that come to the attention of police and are classified as hate crimes. Hate crime incident counts include both confirmed and suspected hate crime incidents.
notes.15: Hate crime, organized crime and cybercrime data from the Uniform Crime Reporting (UCR) Survey are now revised back one year with each annual release. This approach was introduced for the 2019 data release and was applied to the 2018 revised data.
notes.16: It is important to note that while official police-reported data on crime from the Uniform Crime Reporting (UCR) Survey use Statistics Canada's standard Census Metropolitan Area (CMA) names, the boundaries for the policing-based CMAs do not always fully align with the standard CMA geographic units used for disseminating information about the Census of Population.
notes.17: Under the authority of the Canadian Forces Provost Marshal (CFPM), the Canadian Forces Military Police Group (CF MP Gp) is now reporting incidents to the Uniform Crime Reporting (UCR) Survey. They have provided incidents going back to January 2020 and are not included in 2025. Data from the Office of the CFPM are aggregated at the national level to account for small counts and to protect confidentiality. Therefore, provincial and territorial totals will not equal Canada-level totals. Crime Severity Index data and rates are not available.
notes.18: The census metropolitan area (CMA) of Belleville-Quinte West was formerly known as Belleville.
notes.19: The increase in hate crime incidents observed in Halifax beginning in 2023 can be attributed, in part, to the establishment of a dedicated hate crimes unit in Halifax resulting in higher reporting and increased public awareness. For more information visit: https://humanrights.novascotia.ca/news-events/events/understanding-hate-crimes
notes.22: Saint John Police Force hate crime data are unverified for the years they are included (prior to 2023) and therefore represent incidents that are suspected hate crimes only and should be interpreted with caution.
